name: Batham Gate Roman road near Smalldale
status: Modern road follows the Roman line
text: A stretch of today’s road near Smalldale follows Batham Gate. The Roman road connected the warm springs at Buxton with the fort at Brough in the Hope Valley.

name: Batham Gate Roman road in Bradwell parish
text: A low bank in Bradwell parish marks part of Batham Gate. Archaeologists recorded limestone paving elsewhere on this stretch of the Roman road between Buxton and Brough.

name: Watling Street Roman road near High Cross
status: Modern road follows the Roman line
text: The A5 follows Watling Street on this stretch of the Warwickshire and Leicestershire boundary. At nearby High Cross, travellers on Watling Street met another major Roman road, the Fosse Way.

name: Watling Street Roman road near Kilsby
text: This section of Watling Street survives as a green lane between Kilsby and Crick. It escaped the paving that covered other parts of the Roman route, and excavations have investigated its construction.

name: Dere Street Roman road near Soutra
text: On the moor near Soutra, grassy banks preserve part of Dere Street. Roman troops used this route through southern Scotland, and centuries later Edward I’s army followed it on the way to Falkirk.

name: Sarn Helen Roman road near Coelbren
text: East of Coelbren, a track skirts the northern edge of Coed y Rhaiadr. It preserves part of Sarn Helen, the Roman route between Neath and Brecon.
